description: Shared gitignore-semantics corpus. Every verdict here was taken from real `git check-ignore` with `core.excludesFile=/dev/null`. Read by tests/test_scope_exclusions.py (asserts Python pathspec.GitIgnoreSpec agrees) and by momus/extensions/readonly-tools.test.ts (asserts the vendored matcher in readonly-tools.ts agrees). Momus matches paths twice, once per language: the Python diff filter decides what the model reviews, the TypeScript tool layer decides what the model can read. A disagreement between the two matchers is invisible at runtime, so every case here must hold in BOTH suites.
path_convention: Paths are repo-relative and never start with a slash. A trailing slash marks the path as a directory, which is what makes directory-only patterns (`build/`) discriminate.

cases.name: bare filename matches at repo root
bare filename matches at any depth
leading slash anchors to repo root
leading slash does not match a nested copy
trailing slash matches the directory itself
trailing slash matches contents of the directory
trailing slash does not match a plain file of the same name
trailing slash matches a nested directory of that name
anchored directory pattern does not match a nested directory
directory pattern without trailing slash still covers contents
star does not cross a slash
star matches within one segment
double star spans intermediate directories
double star also spans zero directories
leading double star matches at any depth
leading double star matches at the root
interior double star matches zero directories
interior double star matches several directories
interior double star stays anchored at its first segment
a slash in the middle anchors the pattern to the root
a mid-pattern slash blocks matching at depth
negation re-includes a previously excluded file
negation leaves the other matches excluded
negation ordering matters: a later exclude wins
gitignore refuses to re-include under an excluded parent directory
re-include works when the parent directory itself was never excluded
re-include of a sibling under the same parent stays excluded
character class matches each listed character
character class matches the second listed character
character class rejects an unlisted character
character range matches a digit
character range rejects a non-digit

question mark does not match zero characters
empty pattern list excludes nothing
comment lines are not patterns
the momus default list excludes a bundled artifact
the momus default list excludes a nested lockfile
the momus default list keeps test snapshots reviewable
the momus default list keeps ordinary source reviewable
a trailing double-star pattern does not exclude the directory itself
a trailing double-star pattern still excludes the contents
allow-list recipe re-includes a directory excluded by a catch-all
allow-list recipe still excludes everything else
re-including a subdirectory under an excluded parent still fails
a sibling under the same excluded parent stays excluded
a backslash escapes a leading bang
a deep ancestor exclusion blocks a deep re-include

negated character class rejects a listed character

negated multi-character range rejects inside the range

a negation carrying a negated class leaves the excluded character out

unsupported_patterns.reason: Momus rejects these patterns at config load. A POSIX bracket expression is the one construct the Python matcher (pathspec) and the TypeScript matcher (vendored in readonly-tools.ts) read differently, and a disagreement means a file could leave the diff while staying readable, or be blocked from reading while still being reviewed. Measured: for `[[:digit:]]ile.txt`, git ignores `3ile.txt`; pathspec ignores `d]ile.txt` instead, because Python's `re` reads the class as the set `[:digt` followed by a literal `]`; the vendored matcher matches nothing at all. No reading is git's, so momus refuses the pattern and names the reason. Negated character classes are NOT on this list: both matchers agree with git on those, verified against `git check-ignore` over the fuzz corpus, and the `cases` above assert it.
